name: Horus House
subtitle: Party Base of Operations
body:
A three-story narrow rowhouse in the Hive Ward, near the ward border. Horus Lanternholder owned it. Now the party does.

Ground floor: kitchen, common room, a workbench. Second floor: two bedrooms. Third floor: Horus's study and a roof access hatch. Basement: trapdoor under a kitchen rug, crates of supplies and magical items including the bag of withholding.

The house is in decent repair. Horus kept it functional rather than comfortable. There is food in the kitchen. There is a lock on the front door. The lock is better than the neighborhood suggests.

callout.label: NEW HAVEN PORTAL
callout.text: The house connects to New Haven via a portal in the study. Four conditions required: roof, invited host, shared meal, spoken welcome. As Horus's household, the party satisfies conditions 1–3 automatically when one member cooks from house supplies. They must still speak the welcome.

name: The Mortuary
subtitle: Dustmen Headquarters, Sigil Corpse Disposal
body:
The Mortuary is Sigil's official body-processing facility. Every corpse in Sigil comes here, by law. The Dustmen maintain it, staff it, and manage the paperwork that follows every death in the city.

It is large, gray, and smells of preservation chemicals. The staff are professional and slightly offputting. The queue for disposal during high-tension periods can be several days long. The Dustmen do not rush.

The party's first visit follows the Session One combat at Horus House. Three Rusted Bell bodies, no witnesses except the party. The Dustmen require: cause of death, names if known, and the disposal fee (5 gp per body for standard processing). They do not ask difficult questions. They have seen worse.

name: The Gray Ledger (Shop Front)
subtitle: Money-Lending Shop, Gray Ledger Front Operation
body:
A tidy shopfront on a Hive Ward commercial corridor. Sign reads "The Gray Ledger — Loans, Accounts, Exchange." Clean windows, a bell on the door, a queue of ward residents waiting for service.

Wex works the counter. He is pleasant, efficient, and knows exactly what the posted rates are and nothing else. The counting room is one floor up, accessed by a door behind the counter that requires a key Wex does not have.

The shop is legitimate in the way that a front operation is legitimate: the loans are real, the payments are collected, the paperwork is filed. The accounting behind the accounting is where the interesting material is.

callout.label: INVESTIGATION
callout.text: The counting room holds the evidence for Clue 3. DC 15 Perception or Investigation to notice the inconsistency in the posted ledger. DC 20 to access the back records. Drusine is gone before the party gets here.

name: Five Portals Inn
subtitle: Inn and Stables, Lower Ward
body:
The Five Portals Inn sits just inside the Lower Ward border, close enough to the Hive that the clientele skews toward travelers who cannot afford the Lady's Ward and do not want to sleep in the Hive. It is crowded, loud, and functional. The five elemental connections it advertises are real: water flows through the common room, fire burns in an open central hearth, the lamps run bright without oil, a cool breeze moves through the upper corridors at all hours, and the fifth amenity is unmentionable.

Gurand Jor owns it and Katrina Higildra runs the bar. Neither has time for nonsense. Both are the Sigil kind of kind: they will not let a clueless stranger freeze in the street, but do not read warmth into it. They knew Horus. This was not the first time he brought in newcomers who had no idea where they were.

Toloin, Horus's donkey, is stabled out back.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: This is where the campaign starts. The party arrived here, met Horus, and followed him to his house. Gurand and Katrina both know Horus brought clueless before. They will not volunteer information but they will not lie either. The fifth amenity routes waste to the Plane of Mud. It is never explained.

name: The Ninefold Headquarters
subtitle: Ninefold HQ and Ward Portal Site
body:
A converted warehouse in the Hive Ward's interior, claimed by the Ninefold as their central operation. Salt runs meetings from a back office. The main floor is used for goods transit and labor placement — legitimate businesses that the protection operation runs alongside.

One of the nine corridors the Ninefold controls runs directly to a portal site in the warehouse's loading dock. The portal key is a specific knot pattern tied in rope. Salt knows the key. His lieutenants do not.

The warehouse is not comfortable and not designed to be. It is functional: a place where work gets done.

name: The Gatehouse
subtitle: Bleak Cabal Headquarters and Asylum, Hive Ward
body:
The Gatehouse is the headquarters of the Bleak Cabal and Sigil's only asylum. It is a tiered tower of terraces and spires, rising over the Hive's rooftops. Faces peer from the tiny windows at all hours.

The Bleak Cabal believe that the multiverse has no meaning, and that the only sane response is to tend to the suffering around you anyway. The asylum is their proof of principle: a place where the mad, the broken, and the abandoned are housed and cared for without judgment. The staff are volunteers. The conditions are better than you would expect from the ward.

The main gate is open during daylight hours. The inner wards are not accessible without an escort. The Cabal does not turn away visitors who come to pay respects to a patient, but they will not let you wander.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Main gate open by day; inner wards by escort only

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Cabal's nihilism is sincere but not grim in performance. Staff tend to be steady, practical, and low-drama. A party asking for help will not be turned away if they present a genuine need. Useful as a safe harbor and as an information source: the Cabal see more of the Hive than any other faction.

name: The Ditch
subtitle: The Hive Ward's Central Channel
body:
The Ditch is a wide, slow channel of foul water that cuts through the Hive Ward. It is not a river: nothing feeds it and nothing drains it at any visible rate. It is simply there, full of refuse, the occasional corpse, and a population of things that prefer not to be identified.

A few low bridges cross it. The banks are occupied by the people who have nowhere else to go. The smell carries several streets in any direction.

Despite its condition, the Ditch is a landmark. Residents navigate by it. The Certified Fishing Circle operates on its eastern bank. The Gatehouse Night Market sets up nearby after dark. It is, in its way, the center of the Hive.

stats.label: Notable
stats.value: Fishing Circle (east bank), Night Market (nearby after dark)

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Ditch is a useful encounter spine. At any hour there are people here who have no better place to be. By night it is darker and more dangerous. Parakk the Ratcatcher is said to work the streets across from the Bottle and Jug, one block from the east bank.

name: Gatehouse Night Market
subtitle: After-Dark Market, Hive Ward
body:
The Night Market sets up in the shadow of the Gatehouse after dark, filling the alley and yard space that sits empty during the day. Vendors appear from nowhere, lay out their goods on blankets or crates, and are gone before first light. No one asks names. No one makes change. No one asks where anything came from.

Prices are low. Quality is uncertain. The selection covers anything that cannot be sold in daylight: stolen goods, restricted materials, information by the whisper, services that do not benefit from witnesses. The Bleak Cabal ignores it. The Harmonium does not come here at night.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Night Market is a good source for things the party cannot buy through legitimate channels: black-market components, fenced items, rumors for sale, contacts who do not want to be found. Roll a d6 for what is available on any given night. The vendors do not carry standing inventory: what is here tonight is gone tomorrow.

name: Fell's Tattoo Shop
subtitle: Tattoo Parlor, Redwind Road, Hive Ward
body:
A rounded building on Redwind Road, marked by a sign of a black lightning bolt in a white oval. The sign moves. So do the tattoos on anyone who has sat in Fell's chair.

Fell is a dabus, one of the Lady of Pain's silent servants, working independently. He communicates in the dabus manner: rebuses of images and symbols that drift and fade above his head. He does not speak. He does not need to. His needlework is done without words and the results are unambiguous.

The tattoos Fell applies are not merely decorative. At his discretion, he can render an image in a way that allows it to temporarily become a real object. This ability is not advertised. He does not use it for everyone and will not explain the criteria. At night he is sometimes seen bricking up ooze portals in the Hive's alleys, a habit no one has successfully explained.

stats.label: Sign
stats.value: Black lightning bolt in white oval

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Source: Uncaged: Faces of Sigil (TSR 2624), pp. 36-37. The book places Fell in the Market/Guildhall Ward; the 5e map places him in the Hive Ward. Hive Ward is canon for this campaign. Fell is a neutral contact: not an enemy, not a reliable ally. He will tattoo the party if they ask and can pay. Whether and when a tattoo becomes real is entirely at his discretion and yours.

name: Smoldering Corpse Bar
subtitle: Bar, Hive Ward
body:
A low, domed building whose chimneys never stop smoking and whose blood-stained metal tables are never empty. The name is literal: the centerpiece of the main room is an immolated figure suspended mid-air, perpetually burning without being consumed. This is considered normal decor.

The Smoldering Corpse is a gathering place for the Hive's more dangerous residents. Fiends, undead, and beings who would not be welcome elsewhere are welcome here. The bartender has seen worse than you. So has everyone at the bar.

The back room belongs to the Cask Family.

stats.label: Notable
stats.value: Cask Family HQ in back room

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Cask Family uses the back room for collections and planning, not for public meetings. A party entering uninvited finds it locked and guarded. The front bar is accessible to anyone who can pay and behave (by Hive standards). The floating burning figure is real. No one knows who it was.

name: Parakk Pest
subtitle: Tavern and Pest Control Service, Hive Ward
body:
A tall, terraced metal building topped with a giant rat skull. The skull is real. The menu is questionable and questions are offensive.

Parakk the Ratcatcher lives here, or nearby, depending on when you ask. He is a githzerai who has named himself after his trade: the word means both servant and master in his tongue. He works alone, he works at odd hours, and he does not explain himself. His method involves sending unwanted pests through a shifting portal to a pocket demiplane, leaving them adrift in the Deep Ethereal. He calls this kinder than what they deserve.

He can be hired. He can be found by asking at the Bottle and Jug, one block from the east bank of the Ditch.

stats.label: Services
stats.value: Pest removal (via portal to pocket demiplane)

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Source: Uncaged: Faces of Sigil (TSR 2624), pp. 76-77. Parakk is introverted and quietly desperate. He works for the Us (a cranium rat collective) and is trying to free them from Ilsensine's control. He will not discuss this. He avoids combat. If cornered he uses cranium rats and his plane shift ability to escape. The portal to the pocket demiplane is a possible plot hook: things sent there do not come back.

name: Bottle and Jug
subtitle: Tavern, Hive Ward
body:
A round tower of black granite with a tall arched door. The Bottle and Jug is one of the larger taverns in the Hive, known for nightly entertainment combat: staged fights on a raised platform, with the crowd betting on outcomes. The fighters are professionals, mostly. The outcomes are not always staged.

The alley entrance to the Rusted Bell's basement hangout is around the side of the building, unmarked.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Bottle and Jug is where you send the party when they need to find someone in the Hive. Parakk can be found by asking here. The Rusted Bell has their own entrance; Bottle and Jug staff know about it but do not advertise it. The nightly fights are real and the betting is real: a source of income and a time sink if the party gets interested.

name: Grease Pit
subtitle: Food Market, Hive Ward
body:
A wide ring-shaped pit at the edge of the district, packed with food stalls on all sides. A central table area occupies the floor of the pit. The selection is broad by Hive standards: a wide range of foods and beverages, most of them cheap, some of them identifiable. The vendors are permanent fixtures and treat the pit as their territory.

The Grease Pit is the closest thing the Hive has to a public dining hall. It is crowded at most hours. It is not clean. It is affordable, and in this ward that counts for more than cleanliness.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: A good location for eavesdropping, low-stakes contact meetings, and picking up Hive-level street information. The vendors are locals and know the ward. A party eating here will not be notable; a party asking questions will be.

name: Cask Family HQ
subtitle: Cask Family Back Room, Smoldering Corpse Bar, Hive Ward
body:
The Cask Family's operational center is the back room of the Smoldering Corpse Bar, reached through twisting hallways past the main bar. The door is locked. There is a guard.

The room is used for collections, planning, and meetings that the Cask Family prefers not to hold in public. It is not large. It is not comfortable. It is functional, which is more than most of the Hive offers.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Through Smoldering Corpse Bar, locked door, guarded

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Cask Family runs protection and debt collection in the Hive. The back room is their territory; walking in uninvited is a serious provocation. The party will interact with the Cask Family through the Hive arc tension track. This location becomes accessible if they reach terms with the Family or if they are running a job for them.

name: Ninefold Tenement
subtitle: Ninefold Territorial Marker, Ditch East Bank, Hive Ward
body:
A collapsed tenement in a courtyard on the Ditch's east bank, at the edge of the Night Market. The Ninefold have claimed the site and use it as a territorial marker: a base for their ward-level operations, a checkpoint on who moves through this corner of the Hive at night.

The building's collapse has not been repaired. The rubble has been arranged to create defensible positions. Someone always seems to be here, even when the place looks empty.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: This is the Ninefold's street presence, separate from their warehouse HQ. They watch the Night Market from here and enforce their tax on vendors. A party dealing with the Ninefold arc will pass through this location. It is not a place for confrontation: the defensive positions are real and the Ninefold outnumber most parties in this ward.

name: Rusted Bell Hangout
subtitle: Rusted Bell Gang Basement, Bottle and Jug, Hive Ward
body:
The Rusted Bell's main gathering space is in the basement of the Bottle and Jug, accessible only through an unmarked alley entrance on the side of the building. The basement entrance is not advertised. The Bottle and Jug staff do not ask about it.

This is where the Rusted Bell plans, drinks, and argues. It is not a welcoming space for outsiders. The gang uses it because it is cheap, private, and attached to a bar.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Alley entrance, side of Bottle and Jug

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Rusted Bell are the gang that attacked Horus in Session 1. The party disposed of three of their members. The gang does not know who was responsible yet. This basement is where they would be found if the party pursues that thread. It is not a fortified position but it is on the gang's home ground, so they will be confident here.

name: Certified Fishing Circle of the Ditch
subtitle: The Only Credentialed Fishing Spot in Sigil, Hive Ward
body:
The only credentialed fishing spot in all of Sigil. The certification is from an authority whose name has been lost. The fish are real, though their nature is disputed. Rods for rent. Bait for sale. Regulars welcome.

It sits on the east bank of the Ditch, next to the water and the smell. The regulars are there most mornings and some evenings. They do not catch much. They are not primarily here to catch fish.

stats.label: Equipment
stats.value: Rods for rent; bait for sale

stats.label: Catch
stats.value: Variable; identification of catch not guaranteed

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Fishing Circle is live and visible on the map. It is a contact point and a low-key location for conversations the party does not want overheard. The regulars are neighborhood fixtures who know more about Ditch-side Hive activity than they let on. Treat them as a passive information resource: buy bait, start talking.

name: Boneyard Pond
subtitle: Still Pond, Hive Ward
body:
A still pond of uncertain origin somewhere in the Hive's interior, far enough from main streets that only regulars know the approach. The surface is covered in floating refuse and the occasional corpse. Someone is usually on the shore, trying to find a drink or a place to sit without being moved along.

It is not clean, not safe, and not managed by anyone. It persists anyway, as things in the Hive tend to.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Known to locals; not on main streets

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: A good location for a clandestine meeting or a body disposal that someone will notice too late. The regulars here are the bottom tier of the Hive's social structure. They are not dangerous but they are observant: if you do something here, someone saw it.

name: Scratch Wall
subtitle: Public Message Wall, Hive Ward
body:
A wall covered in scratched messages from floor to ceiling, in a dozen languages and twice as many hands. Press a copper coin to it and it will take your words, scratching them into the stone. The message remains until it is covered by a newer one or until the reader presses their own coin to read a specific mark.

The Scratch Wall is the Hive's public forum. Job offers, threats, meeting requests, declarations of love, and information for sale are all here, compressed into stone. Knowing how to read it is a skill. Finding a specific message requires time, a coin, and patience.

stats.label: Cost
stats.value: 1 cp to post; 1 cp to read a specific mark

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Scratch Wall is an in-world mechanism for delivering information to the party or seeding rumors. A party checking the wall can find anything you have planted there. Use it for job offers, faction messages, or clues. Reading requires a copper and a DC 12 Investigation check to find a specific message in the mass of text; DC 8 to find anything at all relevant to a given topic.

name: Granny Nettle's
subtitle: Corner Shop, Hive Ward
body:
A cottage on a Hive Ward corner that looks like it could fall apart at any moment. A closer look shows the wood is well made, the nails well placed, and the roof well thatched. Someone has put careful work into making it look worse than it is.

The sign, where visible, reads: Wools, Silks, and Custom Imports, Inc. The goods in the window suggest a wider inventory than the sign implies.

stats.label: Condition
stats.value: Deceptively sturdy; worse-looking than it is

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Granny Nettle is the Hive arc's hag shop. The player-facing card stays plain. The shop's real inventory and Nettle's role in the arc are in your DM notes only: the Arc 1 doc and the hive arc tension track. The building's solid construction is not a coincidence.
